name: Workshop - Meridian Bank (Attrition & Next-Best-Action)
narrative:
Marcus Bell, a non-technical EVP of Consumer & Small Business Banking, opens his relationship-manager console and sees the same thing his RMs have been feeling for three weeks: a cluster of the bank's most valuable customers glowing red — high balances, long tenure, and an attrition-risk score that has climbed sharply since a competitor launched a savings-rate promotion aimed squarely at maturing CDs. The overnight extract the RMs work from can't see it until the money has already walked.

He asks about the worst account: customer CUST-0000214, a 12-year relationship with a large CD maturing in nine days and a risk score of 0.86 — what is the next best action? The assistant ranks the three plays (match the competitor rate to retain the CD, cross-sell a product the customer qualifies for but doesn't hold, or queue a relationship-manager outreach call), each with cost, the customer's expected lifetime value at stake, and predicted retained revenue from a heuristic scored on Meridian's own retention history. It recommends the rate-match retention offer, drafts the outreach note, and stops for approval. Marcus approves; the action writes back to Lakebase with an audit trail an examiner could follow — governed customer-360 data turned into a relationship action, with the assistant's AI spend capped and attributable per line of business, and no broad PII exposure.

Workshop training template (Tech Summit FY27 Live Days): data generator + full spec set (SDP pipeline, metric views, next-best-action model, dashboard + Genie, and a Databricks App with a Visualize/Assist/Act agent loop over Lakebase). Maps to the three build milestones — Lakebase, Databricks Apps, Unity AI Gateway.
